rules.scoring: Every scored criterion uses its official 0-4 descriptors unchanged; a level never scores part of a criterion.
rules.handwritten_rule: EE19 and EE20 are scored only from handwritten evidence (the original sheet or an image of it). For a typed submission they are recorded as not_evaluable with reason handwritten_evidence_required.

levels.purpose: Linguistic conventions in a short text the student writes or corrects.
levels.notes: An exercise targets one or more convention criteria. The descriptor counts the non-normative uses that remain in the student's final text; the rubric note on identical repetitions applies.

levels.purpose: From a topic and communicative situation, state a main idea and at least two complementary ideas in an introduction paragraph.
levels.notes: The paragraph is an introduction, so EE04 applies with its full descriptors; EE03 judges digressions in that paragraph.

levels.purpose: Write the development paragraphs (causes and consequences) or the conclusion paragraph (actions or solutions).
levels.notes: development_paragraphs asks for exactly two paragraphs (EE05); conclusion_paragraph for one (EE06).

levels.purpose: A complete four-paragraph expository text with scaffolding (paragraph plan, suggested ideas and connectors); no time limit.
levels.notes: Scaffolding changes the support, not the criteria.

levels.purpose: The national-test task: an expository text of four paragraphs and 200 words in 90 minutes, without scaffolding beyond the suggested ideas.
levels.notes: Handwritten evidence is the exam condition (ballpoint pen, blue or black ink). A typed rehearsal targets all 20 criteria but records EE19 and EE20 as not_evaluable.
